chunks: 9. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Sari, from Jabir ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

regarding something of Divine Unity, he said: Verily, Allah – Blessed are His Names by which He is called upon and Exalted is He in the loftiness of His Essence – is One, United in Oneness in the loftiness of His Unity, then He applied it to His creation, so He is One, Samad (Needless), Quddus (Most Holy), everything worships Him and everything depends upon Him, and His Knowledge encompasses everything.

key_terms.صَمَدٌ: The Everlasting, the One upon whom all depend
key_terms.يُصْمِدُ إِلَيْهِ: Depends upon Him / Turns to Him

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Divine Unity (Tawhid) according to Imam al-Baqir (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the ontological oneness of Allah, emphasizing that His absolute unity transcends creation while simultaneously being the focal point of all existence's worship and reliance. The Imam highlights Allah's attributes of *Samad* (the Eternal Refuge) and *Quddus* (the Holy), noting that every entity both worships Him and turns to Him, underscoring His all-encompassing knowledge. This explanation serves as a foundational commentary on Surah Al-Ikhlas, bridging the metaphysical concept of Tawhid with its practical manifestation in the cosmos.
